I knew early on I was not alone in my experience, but somehow it still felt lonely. There was lots of grief and tears involved in the process. Vasospasm and nipple blisters were a nightmare, undetected lip and tongue tie did not help. Numerous appointments with lactation clinic, and finally finding paid specialists is what helped, but at that point my supply was already dwindling. So much time spent at the breast that I felt like a cow, and not a person, and was constantly told that everything was fine… how women do this without any support I will never know.

I legitimately have PTSD from my first. He had a painful latch that never really resolved despite a lot of support, so after 6 months of trying to exclusively nurse, I ended up exclusively pumping for another 8 months. I felt so lonely, desperate, and helpless, and all my friends having babies seemed to have no problems with nursing. In the end, I feel good about our journey, but it took a lot for me to get there. Now my second baby is almost 6 months old and still going strong with nursing, but she also needed a lot of help in the beginning. So much love to all the mamas struggling. It really is its own special kind of hell to have feeding struggles. Whatever you need to do to feed your baby really is okay, even though it doesn’t seem that way at the time.

It threw me off at first, until it didn’t. I quickly remembered that my sister in law, Jordan, was breastfeeding their now 3 month old baby, and reached out to her to see if she had a stash of milk that she would be willing to share with us. She had been building a stash for a vacation that was coming up but selflessly gave it to us 😭 
It kept Lux fed in those early days and took a ton of stress off my shoulders because I knew Lux was getting the best nutrition possible, even if it wasn’t from me specifically. I loved the peace that provided, so with my lactation consultant’s help, found another donor, someone local with an oversupply who had milk to give. The donor milk has been keeping us afloat while I continue trying to get my supply up. The donor milk eventually runs out though, so my days as a new mom are spent feeding Lux from my breast and bottles, pumping, hand expressing, and checking our local milk sharing Facebook pages networking with other mamas to try & find the next batch of donor milk. It sounds like a lot, and it is - but it’s the solution I’m most comfortable with for now. I realize there are other ways to feed him and those may be in our future but for now, this is our chosen path. There’s a special kind of pain that only moms with a low supply know. But to see how women rally around other women to help when this happens, share their own precious milk with a sister or even a perfect stranger, lend a supportive ear, and share their own stories and struggles so you don’t feel so alone - is the silver lining for me. It’s an experience I never anticipated but I’ll pony it up to another humbling and eye-opening part of motherhood. One of many more to come, I’m sure.
